TaktX Engine — Deployment & Architecture Overview

Overview

TaktX is a lightweight BPMN engine built as a Java Quarkus application. It uses Apache Kafka as the single source of truth for persistence and storage and relies on Kafka topics to manage process definitions, process state and external tasks like service and send tasks. The engine is shipped today as a Docker image; plain JAR and native builds are planned for future releases.

Kafka for persistence and storage

  • All runtime state and task events are persisted to Kafka topics. Kafka acts as the durable event log and recovery store.
  • Events and task messages are retained in Kafka so instances can replay stream data to reconstruct state after restarts or join the cluster at any time.
  • Offset commits and topic durability provide recovery semantics: uncommitted work will be redelivered after consumer failure.

External tasks and topic model

  • External tasks (for example: service tasks, send tasks) are organized by job id. Each job id has its own Kafka topic.
  • Topics are managed dynamically: when the engine detects a new job id it will create and start using a topic for that job id.
  • The engine publishes task triggers into that per-job topic and worker instances consume from it. This isolates task types and simplifies routing and scaling.
  • Topics are partitioned. Parallelism for a job id is achieved by adding partitions; each partition is consumed by at most one consumer instance in a consumer group.

Deployment and distribution

  • Implementation: Java + Quarkus.
  • Current distribution: Docker image only. Run the image in your container platform and point it at your Kafka cluster, or use the provided docker-compose file which includes a Kafka installation
  • Upcoming distributions: plain executable JAR and GraalVM native builds (smaller footprint and faster startup) will be provided in future releases.

Horizontal scalability

  • Scale-out model: run multiple TaktX engine instances that all connect to the same Kafka cluster.
  • Per-job parallelism: increase the number of partitions on a job topic; add more engine instances. Kafka will assign partitions across instances, enabling concurrent processing of tasks for that job id.
  • Work distribution: client instances join the same Kafka consumer group for a given job topic. Kafka’s partition assignment guarantees exclusive consumption per partition, avoiding duplicate concurrent processing of the same partition.
  • Recommended practice: increase partitions to match desired parallelism and then add instances. Partitions are the unit of parallel work.
